scope: Base · Male (build/q309/viewer_zan_atlas, key base_m) and Base · Female (build/q309/viewer_base_female, key base_f) only

doc.what: Selectable parts (heads, parts, fibre groups) of large or multi-part muscles, and how each maps onto the Base pages.
doc.schema: muscles[]: {muscle_id (repo record base id, or a group id such as erector_spinae), name, region, whole_muscle_structures (page ids per body and side, or null when the page has only the parts), parts[], contested, note}. parts[]: {id, name, ta_latin (Terminologia Anatomica Latin part name where standard, else null), origin, nerve_supply, nerve_source[], refs[] (keys into references), verification (verified = opened PubMed record; verified_book = attachment / nerve read in an opened book, Q348; unverified_textbook = textbook, page not checked), note, book_q348 {ref, page, fact, rule_check}?, body}. body: {status, structures {base_m|base_f: {r:[], l:[], mid:[]}}, rule?, reason?, note?}. status: separate_mesh | separate_mesh_rule_based | rule | not_delimitable | missing_on_page. rule.name is a key of rules{}; every rule is a PROPOSAL (validated=false) and must be validated before a part is drawn.
doc.ui: Parts chooser: offer "whole muscle" + each part. separate_mesh -> select those ids. separate_mesh_rule_based -> select, keep the rule badge. rule -> show greyed with "rule-based, not validated" until an implementation passes its validation_plan; then draw with a rule-based badge citing the rule + refs. not_delimitable -> list the part (name, nerve, source) without geometry. Side: use the clicked structure's side; ids are given per side.
doc.honesty: No geometry was made here. Rules are written out so an implementer can test them; the project rejected a deltoid sector rule after validation (q219_validation), so none of these rules may be shown as anatomy before it is validated.

separate_mesh.label: Separate structure on the page
separate_mesh.method: The part is its own mesh on the page (a Z-Anatomy part object, fitted with the body). Select the listed ids; no rule needed.
separate_mesh.error: as the page mesh (its own fit badge)

separate_mesh_rule_based.label: Separate rule-based structure on the page
separate_mesh_rule_based.method: The part is its own mesh, but that mesh was itself built by a documented rule (see its badge on the page). Selectable; keep its rule-based badge visible.

fan_projection_from_insertion.label: Fan projection from the insertion (convergent muscle)
fan_projection_from_insertion.method: For a muscle whose fibres converge on a compact insertion: take the centroid I of the insertion footprint (data/derived/Q220_parts_zbase_{m,f}.json insertion placement, else the contact patch on the insertion bone). For every vertex v of the muscle mesh, extend the ray I->v until it meets the origin footprint (the band where the mesh touches its origin bones / fascia). v belongs to the part whose named origin segment that ray reaches. Origin segments are the sourced ones listed in the part rows (e.g. latissimus dorsi: spinous processes T7-T12 + thoracolumbar fascia | iliac crest | lower ribs | inferior angle of scapula). Boundaries between segments are the named bony landmarks on the page (vertebra / rib / iliac-crest / scapula meshes).
fan_projection_from_insertion.validation_plan: Leave-one-out against the three Z-Anatomy pectoralis major part meshes (clavicular / sternocostal / abdominal: origin segments clavicle | sternum + costal cartilages | rectus sheath) on both Base bodies; report vertex accuracy and centroid error. The deltoid azimuth rule failed this kind of test (q219_validation); do not display a fan partition until it passes.

boundary_fibre_plane.label: Boundary-fibre plane (fan with a long insertion)
boundary_fibre_plane.method: Where both origin and insertion are long lines and the parts are defined by consecutive origin segments: the boundary between two parts is the fibre running from the origin boundary landmark O_b to the insertion boundary landmark I_b. The cut is the plane through O_b and I_b that also contains the local surface normal of the muscle sheet at the midpoint (for a back muscle the body's antero-posterior axis). Vertices are assigned by the side of the plane.
boundary_fibre_plane.validation_plan: No Z part meshes exist for trapezius or adductor magnus parts to validate against; show only as an explicitly rule-based overlay, never as anatomy.
boundary_fibre_plane.error: unknown; fibres are not straight lines on a curved sheet

two_belly_axial_split.label: Two side-by-side bellies split along the muscle axis
two_belly_axial_split.method: Fit the principal axis of the muscle mesh (PCA). Cut by the plane that contains this axis and the antero-posterior direction of the limb segment; the named head on each side is the textbook topography (biceps brachii: long head lateral, short head medial; gastrocnemius: medial head medial, lateral head lateral).
two_belly_axial_split.validation_plan: No Z part meshes for these heads; heads are unequal in size (gastrocnemius medial head larger and longer), so a mid-plane is known to be approximate.

transverse_level_planes.label: Transverse planes at named levels
transverse_level_planes.method: Cut the mesh by planes perpendicular to the body long axis (+Y) at named bony levels given in the part rows.
transverse_level_planes.validation_plan: Check against visible tendinous intersections on the mesh if the mesh shows them; otherwise display as rule-based only.
transverse_level_planes.error: the textbook levels are typical, not individual

nearest_origin_bone_lower_segment.label: Nearest origin bone (only where the heads are still separate)
nearest_origin_bone_lower_segment.method: For two heads that arise from different bones and fuse further along: within the segment where the heads are separate (between the origin and the point where they meet), each vertex goes to the head whose origin bone contact patch is nearer along the muscle axis. Above the fusion level the vertices are not assigned to a head.
nearest_origin_bone_lower_segment.validation_plan: No Z part meshes; the fusion level is not sourced numerically -> coverage incomplete by design.

not_delimitable.label: Not delimitable honestly on this mesh
not_delimitable.method: The parts are layers (superficial / deep), are defined by fibre direction or by intramuscular septa that the mesh does not show, or the opened sources give no boundary. Listing the part (name, nerve, source) is fine; drawing it would be invented geometry.
